facts.text: Midtown’s cultural heart sits on Woodward, where the Detroit Public Library Main Branch and the Detroit Institute of Arts were built in the 1920s City Beautiful movement.
The Art Center Historic District in Midtown centers on the library, the DIA, and the Horace H. museum, forming a cohesive cultural enclave.
About 80 original homes survive in Midtown, many listed on the National Register of Historic Places, showcasing the neighborhood’s architectural heritage.
Midtown was first platted after Detroit’s 1805 fire, with Congress authorizing a new village north of the city along Woodward Avenue.
In the 1950s and 60s, Wayne State University expanded into Midtown’s northwest, rehabilitating historic buildings and adding new academic spaces.
The Cass Corridor, spanning Woodward westward to the Lodge Freeway, has been a hub of artistic and countercultural activity since the 1960s.
